findings.claim: For the Eduqas exam, understanding both the potential and the current limitations of these approaches is what separates a Mastering from a Secure response on a sustainability question.
findings.truth: House rule: an Eduqas/WJEC lesson must never name the exam board in student-facing prose. Neutral phrasing is 'the exam' or 'this paper'.
findings.evidence: house rule in the checker brief; only instance of a board name in the unit

findings.claim: Examiners reward this kind of nuanced, balanced analysis throughout your answer.
findings.truth: A claim about what examiners reward is not supported by the spec or by any published mark scheme. The advice itself is sound; the appeal to examiners is invented.
findings.evidence: spec assessment description (written examination, 2 hours, 100 marks) states no such reward rule

findings.claim: Example: 50 million PET drinks bottles produced per day worldwide.
findings.truth: About 480 billion plastic drinks bottles were sold in 2017, which is roughly 1.3 billion a day. The lesson figure is about 26 times too low.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Plastic bottle (480 billion sold in 2017; about a million a minute); recomputation 480e9/365 = 1.3e9 per day

findings.claim: PHA requires specific anaerobic soil or marine conditions
findings.truth: PHA does not need anaerobic conditions. It breaks down in soil and in seawater, both of which are aerobic. Lesson 2 of this unit already says PHA breaks down in soil and marine environments, so the two lessons contradict each other.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with L2 content_html; seawater and topsoil are aerobic environments

findings.claim: uPVC is the most commonly extruded polymer (window and door frames), but polyethylene, polypropylene and nylon are also widely extruded.
findings.truth: Polyethylene is produced in about three times the tonnage of PVC and most of it is extruded as film, pipe and sheet. uPVC is widely extruded but it is not the most extruded polymer.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Plastic (2015 production: LDPE 64 Mt + HDPE 52 Mt = 116 Mt, 28.5%; PVC 38 Mt, 9.3%)

findings.claim: Question [1] asks only 'Name the shaping process used for thermosetting polymers such as urea formaldehyde.' but is set at 2 marks, and its mark scheme awards the second mark for a brief description of the process.
findings.truth: A student who answers exactly what is asked, with the two words 'compression moulding', can only reach 1 of the 2 marks. The question stem must ask for the description the mark scheme pays for.
findings.evidence: the question's own mark scheme text

findings.claim: hot gas welding (a plastics welder directs a stream of hot air onto the joint and a matching filler rod while the surfaces are pressed together - used for PVC pipes, boat hulls and chemical storage tanks)
findings.truth: Boat hulls are a poor example here. Lesson 1 of this unit correctly teaches that boat hulls are made from polyester resin, a thermoset, which cannot be welded. Hot gas welding joins thermoplastic sheet: pipe, ducting, pond liners and tanks.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with L1 content_html (polyester resin - boat hulls); plastic welding works only on thermoplastics, as this same paragraph states

findings.claim: The bonded joint is often stronger than the surrounding material.
findings.truth: A solvent-cemented joint is the same polymer, but with residual solvent, voids and locked-in stress, so it should not exceed the parent strength. Manufacturers claim it approaches parent strength. No settled published value was found, so no edit is made.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Solvent welding - gives no strength comparison

findings.claim: All other major processes (vacuum forming, injection moulding, blow moulding, extrusion, rotomoulding, FDM) are used for thermoforming polymers only.
findings.truth: Thermoset injection moulding and thermoset extrusion do exist in industry. The absolute statement is the standard GCSE simplification, matches the spec's own pairing of thermosets with compression moulding, and would be credited, so it is left alone.
findings.evidence: spec in-depth polymers section 5 lists blow moulding, vacuum forming, press moulding and compression moulding

findings.claim: recycled PET bottles cannot be used for new food-contact bottles without significant blending with virgin material (repeated in the 8-mark mark scheme and in a flashcard answer)
findings.truth: Chain degradation on remelting is real, but food-grade rPET is now approved and 100% rPET drinks bottles are sold in the UK. Options: (a) leave all three, as the GCSE point about degradation still stands; (b) soften the collapsible sentence only; (c) soften all three occurrences in step, which needs one text edit, one mark-scheme edit and one flashcard edit.
findings.evidence: UK retail 100% rPET bottles; no spec statement either way
findings.ruling: Leave: GCSE-level simplification, little mark gain.

summary: Seven fixes across lessons 3, 4 and 5: one house-rule board name, one invented examiner claim, a PET bottle output figure about 26 times too low, a wrong anaerobic condition for PHA, an unsupported 'most extruded polymer' superlative, a mis-set example for hot gas welding, and a 2-mark question that only asks for a name. Lessons 1 and 2 are clean; all 25 knowledge-check keys and all six multiple-choice answers across the unit recompute correctly.
